title: X Feed Digest
summary: Coding-agent talk shifted from benchmark chest-thumping to workflow design: external tool ecosystems, persistent sessions, and cleaner orchestration patterns were the strongest practical themes.

AI product competition in the batch was more about economics and reliability than raw model IQ, with Composer 2.5 reviews, GPT-5 coding gains, and quota chatter all pointing at cost-effective throughput as the real battleground.

China-linked market risk showed up in two different layers: semiconductor supply may get looser if Chinese DRAM ramps keep accelerating, while offshore brokerage and crypto users are increasingly focused on tax and reporting exposure after the Futu/Tiger crackdown.
Outside pure AI, the most useful operational updates were a reality check on U.S. immigration-process risk for founders and employees, plus SpaceX's mixed-but-informative Starship test debrief.

items.title: @thsottiaux: External Codex Ecosystem
items.body: OpenAI's Tibo disclosed that roughly 5% of production traffic is already flowing through Pi and another 5% through OpenCode. That's a strong signal that frontier coding products are becoming an ecosystem battle, not just a single-app battle.

items.title: @HooCrypto: Composer 2.5 Field Report
items.body: After 72 hours of heavy use, this review praised Composer 2.5 for unusually strong speed-per-dollar, better web search, and stabler MCP connections, while still wanting it to act more agentically and present tradeoffs. It was one of the better practitioner posts in the batch because it focused on workflow friction instead of vibes.

items.title: @9hills: Long-Lived Agent Sessions
items.body: This workflow tip argued for keeping one persistent session per major feature, pairing it with separate worktrees, and forcing real code and test work into subagents instead of the main thread. It's a practical pattern for getting more out of coding agents over multi-day work without turning the root context into sludge.

items.title: @Chrisgpt: GPT-5 SWE Pro Trend
items.body: A benchmark recap plotted the GPT-5 coding line rising from 50.8% to 58.6% on public SWE Pro over the last ten months. The useful takeaway is that coding-agent capability is still compounding in steady increments, even without a single dramatic leap headline.

items.title: @LiuInTheShadows: China DRAM Supply Shock
items.body: A widely shared semiconductor thesis argued that Chinese DRAM expansion could break the current DDR5 scarcity story by H2 2027, citing former Samsung leadership and early signs of Chinese chips already entering western-branded modules. If that framing is right, one of the cleaner AI-adjacent trades, memory tightness, gets much less comfortable.

items.title: @linwanwan823: CRS 2.0 After Futu/Tiger
items.body: In the wake of the Futu/Tiger/Longbridge scare, this post argued that mainland users are underestimating the reporting side of the problem: CRS 2.0 plus CARF could make offshore brokerage and crypto activity far more legible to tax authorities. The actionable point is that compliance risk may now matter as much as market risk for China-linked accounts.

items.title: @jason_chen998: Hong Kong Microcap Trap
items.body: The feed highlighted Hong Kong-listed 经纬天地 collapsing roughly 90% shortly after joining Southbound Stock Connect, with commentary centering on how quickly mainland money can get trapped in low-float operator-heavy names. Even if you discount some of the drama, it's a sharp reminder to treat newly connect-eligible microcaps as liquidity events, not validation.

items.title: @deedydas: Immigration Policy Reality Check
items.body: Deedy Das pointed people toward an immigration lawyer's analysis because the new green-card processing headlines were creating more panic than clarity. The broader signal is that visa and adjustment logistics are being felt as live operating risk by founders and employees who assumed the process was mostly bureaucratic background noise.

items.title: @SawyerMerritt: Starship Test 12 Debrief
items.body: SpaceX's post-flight summary described a mixed but meaningful test: booster engine issues and a hard splashdown on the first stage, but successful deployment of 20 Starlink simulators plus useful heatshield and re-entry data from Starship. The program still looks willing to trade cleaner recoveries for faster learning on in-space operations and return profiles.

items.title: @lidangzzz: AI Eval Misreadings
items.body: One of the sharper meta-posts in the batch argued that people keep making the same category errors around coding models: over-learning from one anecdotal win, chaining too many models for no reason, and acting like agents have replaced the need to understand software. It's a useful antidote to a lot of the feed's usual AI slop.
